name: Naval Strike Missile (NSM)
operator: Norway, United States (Navy & Marine Corps), Australia, Poland, and others
overview_md:
The Naval Strike Missile (NSM) is Norway's stealthy anti-ship missile and one of the most widely adopted Western sea-skimming weapons of the 2020s — increasingly the common anti-ship round of the U.S. and allied navies and a centrepiece of American plans to turn the first island chain into a missile-defended barrier. Built by Kongsberg (and produced with Raytheon in the United States), it is a subsonic, low-observable missile that trades speed for stealth, smarts and an unusual seeker.

Unlike most anti-ship missiles, the NSM uses a passive imaging-infrared seeker rather than an active radar, so it does not announce itself by emitting, and it carries an onboard target database to recognise and aim at specific parts of a ship. It flies a sea-skimming course with terrain-following over littorals and can perform evasive manoeuvres on final approach, giving it strong survivability against defences despite a modest ~185 km-plus range.

For an analyst, the NSM's significance is its proliferation and its role in U.S. Marine Corps concepts. It arms the U.S. Navy's Littoral Combat Ships and the new Constellation-class frigates, and — mounted on the unmanned NMESIS ground launcher — it gives Marines a mobile, island-based anti-ship capability central to Expeditionary Advanced Base Operations against China. Adopted by Australia, Poland and many others, the NSM has become the connective anti-ship weapon knitting allied sea-denial together across the Indo-Pacific.

additional.guidance: INS/GPS + terrain-reference + passive imaging-IR seeker with target database
additional.launch_platforms: Ships (LCS, Constellation), NMESIS ground launcher, aircraft (JSM variant)
additional.feature: Passive seeker (no radar emission); terminal evasive manoeuvres

variants_json.name: NSM
variants_json.key_changes: Ship- and ground-launched stealth anti-ship missile

variants_json.name: JSM (Joint Strike Missile)
variants_json.key_changes: Air-launched variant sized for the F-35 internal bay

combat_history.event: Fielded on U.S. Navy LCS/Constellation frigates and the USMC NMESIS ground launcher for island sea-denial.
combat_history.significance: Became the U.S./allied common anti-ship missile and a pillar of first-island-chain strategy.

modernization.description: F-35-internal JSM variant and expanding Marine Corps ground-launcher batteries.
modernization.impact: Adds stealth-aircraft and mobile island launch options.

vulnerabilities.description: Shorter-ranged than heavy missiles like LRASM or BrahMos.
vulnerabilities.context: Best for littoral sea-denial, not deep blue-water strike.
Relies on stealth and manoeuvre, not speed.

operational_patterns.typical_deployment: Littoral sea-denial from ships and mobile island-based ground launchers (NMESIS) against surface ships.
operational_patterns.typical_task_group: USN LCS/Constellation frigates; USMC littoral regiments; allied navies.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: LRASM is the long-range air/ship-launched heavy option; NSM is the smaller, widely-fielded littoral weapon.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: The West's new anti-ship missile family.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: China's coastal anti-ship missile is supersonic and longer-ranged; NSM counters with stealth and proliferation.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: Coastal missile duel across the first island chain.

peer_comparisons.key_differences: Japan's truck-launched anti-ship missile fills the same island-denial role.
peer_comparisons.video_angle: How allies are mining the first island chain with missiles.

doctrine.role: Stealthy littoral anti-ship missile for ship- and island-based sea denial.
doctrine.employment: Sea-skimming passive-IR attack from ships and mobile NMESIS ground launchers; F-35-internal JSM variant.
doctrine.design_philosophy: Stealth, a non-emitting seeker and proliferation over range and speed.
doctrine.threat_context: The common allied anti-ship missile and a pillar of U.S. Marine first-island-chain sea-denial against China.
doctrine.comparison_frame: Read against LRASM (heavy), China's YJ-12 and Japan's Type 12 SSM.
